notes.subject: מגן
notes.rationale: מָגֵן is literally 'shield'; renderings split between 'armed man' (KJV) and 'bandit/robber' (ASV, BSB); Bambara keeps 'one who carries a sword'.

notes.subject: מתהלך
notes.rationale: 'one walking about' could be a traveller or a stalking robber; Bambara taamabaga keeps the walking picture, leaving the ambiguity open.

notes.subject: to the sluggard
notes.rationale: Second-person suffixes ('your poverty', 'your want') address the lazy person directly.

translation: I ka dɛgɛya bɛna na i n'a fɔ taamabaga ye, ani i ka bɛnnɛya i n'a fɔ mɔgɔ min bɛ npan ta.
